evidence.quote: we recover a radially resolved magnetic field with a strength of ${\sim}10~{\rm mG}$ between 60 and 120 au

referee_caveats_inferred: Detection rests on small differential line-width ratios at 80 m/s resolution; unmodeled broadening (e.g. vertical structure, back-side emission) is argued against in simulations only
Both morphology models fit equally well and phi_B is unconstrained, so the field orientation claims are weak
Plasma beta is a lower limit from an LTE density bound and refers to the CN layer, not the midplane
Prior ranges and likelihood details are not given, so posterior widths cannot be audited

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Ten execution blocks with three spectral windows at 80 m/s resolution; likely on the order of 100 GB to a few hundred GB raw (rough estimate)
reproducibility.score_reason: Project code, spectral setup, self-calibration solints, imaging robust and MCMC settings are given, and numeric results are listed, but there is no code release and several key settings (priors, likelihood, CASA version, masks, calibrators) are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public availability of the data is not stated in the paper and the custom Zeeman fitting code and priors are not provided, so a faithful redo is not guaranteed.
